notes: ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE - not legal advice. It shows how an EU policy pack is written for OpsPilot. The sources are real; the numbers are example choices. Have every control reviewed by qualified counsel, then set illustrative to false, before relying on it.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act) - in particular human oversight and record-keeping for high-risk AI systems

approvals.note: Supported by the sources: high-risk AI systems are to be designed for effective human oversight, and GDPR Article 22 gives people rights over solely automated significant decisions. Example choices: approval for any automated action on a personal-data system, a 48-hour deadline and escalation after 8 hours.

riskRules.note: Supported by the sources: the AI Act's risk-based approach, and GDPR's extra protection for special category data. Example choice: treating every AI system that processes personal data as high risk in this tool, which is stricter than the UK example on purpose; the AI Act's own high-risk categories are defined by use, not by data type.

recordKeeping.note: Supported by the sources: the AI Act requires logs for high-risk AI systems to be kept for a minimum period, and GDPR's storage limitation principle limits how long personal data is kept. Example choices: 7 years (2555 days) for the audit log and 6 years (2190 days) for documents; check the minimum log period in the AI Act's provisions for deployers.
